texts.label: text
texts.orig: In this paper; we have presented a robust algorithm for handling specific non-linear projections inside the graphics pipeline. Our algorithm works both for direct display of the non-linear projection; fish-eye lens inside a video game, or for indirect use, e.g when rendering a shadow map with paraboloid projection.
texts.text: In this paper; we have presented a robust algorithm for handling specific non-linear projections inside the graphics pipeline. Our algorithm works both for direct display of the non-linear projection; fish-eye lens inside a video game, or for indirect use, e.g when rendering a shadow map with paraboloid projection.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: As with previous work we start by bouding the projection of each shape, then discard extra fragments inside the bounding shape. Our contributions are twofold First: two different methods for bound ing the non-linear projections, one based on triangles that is opti mal in fragments but requires more work in the geometry engine, the other based on quads that is optimal for the geometry engine but can causes more overdraw. Second: mathematical analysis of several non-linear projection methods, where we show that some of them have simple expressions, and thus lend themselves to easy bounding through geometric tools.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Although non-linear projections are slower than linear projections; the extra cost is manageable: As a single non-linear projection can replace up to five projections (in hemicube) , it can even be practical alternative, both for rendering time and memory cost. linear
